_comment: YOUR STANDING TARGET. Copy this file to `hunt_target.json` and edit it — that copy is
gitignored, because what you are aiming at and why is nobody else's business in a public repo.
This is the answer to 'I don't want to ask you every time'. Every run reads this file, so a
goal set once keeps applying: the focus kinds, the cities, the money floor and the date you
need it by. No flags to remember. Change the file, the next hunt changes with it.
Check what is active any time with:  py main.py --target
Turn it off for one run with:       py main.py --now --no-target
Turn it off for good:               set "active": false
FIELD BY FIELD
active      false parks the whole target without you having to delete your settings.
goal        Free text, for your eyes and the brief's header. Not parsed.
by          ISO date you need this resolved by. Opportunities whose deadline falls AFTER
this date are pushed down — they cannot produce an outcome in time.
focus       Kinds to hunt, from filters.focus.KINDS. Applied automatically, so you do not
have to type --focus. A --focus flag still overrides it for one run.
locations   Cities you could actually take, best first. 'remote' counts as a location and
means work-from-home listings match. A role that is in-office in a city NOT on
this list is pushed down, because you cannot be in two places.
min_pay_per_month  Rupees per month. Listings paying less are pushed down; listings that
do not state pay are left alone rather than punished, since most simply omit it.
require_pay true means an explicitly unpaid or pay-unknown listing loses ground too. Leave
it false unless the money is the whole point.
Weights live in config.TARGET_WEIGHTS if you ever want to tune how hard each one pulls.
goal: Paid internship I can do from Mumbai — offer letter in hand before 5 Dec 2026
